turns.doctor_question: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response:
Hi, doctor. Um, well, I guess I'm here because I just... I feel like everything is completely falling apart and I absolutely cannot get my life organized, like, at all. I have my schoolwork, which is already a lot, you know, trying to keep up with classes and everything, but then I also run this little accessories shop—I make and sell these cute little things online, which I love doing—but I just cannot manage both of them at the same time. It's like my brain just short-circuits. 

If you looked at my desk right now, or really my whole room honestly, it's just piles. Literally piles everywhere. I've got all my crafting supplies and beads and wire just mixed in with my assignment notes, and then there are receipts from shipping things out just buried under, like, loose papers and sticky notes with due dates that I probably already missed. I try to sit down and tackle it, but I look at this massive mountain of shop stuff and essay prompts, and I just don't even know what to do first. I just stand there staring at the piles. It's so frustrating because I really care about my shop, and I know I need to do my schoolwork, but the organization part is just... it's impossible for me right now. I just keep moving the same piles from my bed to my desk and back again, and I really need help figuring it out.

symptom_reasoning.S005: The patient explicitly states they cannot get their life organized, describing their inability to manage schoolwork and their shop simultaneously, resulting in disorganized piles of supplies and assignments.

turns.doctor_question: How long have you been struggling with organization and getting started on tasks like this? Has this always been difficult for you, or is this something that's gotten worse recently?
turns.patient_response:
Well, um, if I really think about the exact timeline, it's been a real, massive problem for about... I'd say two years and maybe two months? Yeah, right around two years and two months. Because I remember exactly when it started getting this bad. It was right when I changed schools. 

Before that, I mean, I wasn't exactly the most organized person on the planet, but it wasn't like this total disaster zone that it is now. But then I switched schools, and I started this business program, which I was super excited about, by the way, because of my shop! I thought, you know, this is going to be perfect for my accessories business, I can learn how to scale it and everything. But the new school... it just had way, way less structure. Like, almost none compared to what I was used to. At my old school, the teachers were always on top of you, reminding you about every little thing, "this is due Tuesday," "bring this on Thursday," but here, it's just all on you to figure it out and pace yourself. 

And suddenly I had to manage all these business program requirements, which are super heavy on reading and long-term projects, and at the exact same time, my shop started getting a little more popular. Which is great! But it also means more orders and more supplies and more shipping runs. And without that rigid, minute-by-minute schedule I used to have forced on me, I just... everything just started bleeding together into these giant piles I was telling you about. So yeah, for the last two years and a couple of months, it's just been this huge uphill battle where I feel like I'm constantly drowning in beads and business plans because nobody is telling me exactly when to do what anymore, and I just can't seem to impose that structure on myself, no matter how hard I try.

symptom_reasoning.S005: The patient explicitly describes a severe inability to organize tasks, manage requirements, and impose structure on themselves, resulting in 'giant piles' and feeling like they are 'drowning'.

turns.doctor_question: When you were younger, say in elementary school or middle school, did you have similar kinds of problems with paying attention, staying organized, or sitting still? Or is this organizational and focus problem something that really only started around the time you changed schools?
turns.patient_response:
Oh, gosh, no, no, it definitely wasn't just when I changed schools. I mean, the piles and the total inability to manage the shop and the homework, that's new, but the... the other stuff? The not sitting still and the focus things? That's been there forever. Like, literally since I was a little kid. 

Actually, it's so funny you ask about elementary school because my mom—she's one of those moms who keeps absolutely everything, like every single piece of paper I ever brought home—she still has all my old report cards and notes from my teachers. And if you look at them, it's honestly kind of embarrassing now, but every single year, the comments were exactly the same. It was always, always about how I couldn't stay in my seat. Like, "She's a sweet girl, but she wanders around the classroom during quiet reading time," or "She needs constant reminders to stay at her desk." I just couldn't do it. My legs would just feel like they had to move, you know? 

And the talking! Oh my gosh, I was always getting in trouble for talking out of turn. The teachers would be in the middle of asking a question, and I'd just blurt out the answer before they even finished the sentence, or before they called on me. I just... the thought would pop into my head and it had to come out of my mouth right that exact second or I felt like I was going to explode. And it wasn't even that I didn't know the material! I actually understood the work fine most of the time, but when we had to do group activities or projects, I would just rush through everything. I'd be like, "Okay, let's do this, this, and this, done!" and my group members would be so annoyed because I was just speeding through it without really taking the time to do it neatly or properly. I just wanted to get to the next thing, and the next thing, and the next thing. So yeah, I guess the business program just kind of exposed it in a new way, but the whole... being unable to just sit and be calm and focus on one thing at a normal pace? That's been happening since I was like, six years old. My mom could probably bring in a whole binder of proof if you wanted to see it!

symptom_reasoning.S001: The patient describes rushing through group activities and speeding through work without taking the time to do it neatly or properly.
symptom_reasoning.S011: The patient explicitly states she could not stay in her seat and would wander around the classroom when she was expected to remain at her desk.
symptom_reasoning.S012: The patient describes a physical sense of restlessness, noting that her legs felt like they just had to move.
symptom_reasoning.S013: The patient mentions being unable to just sit and be calm.
symptom_reasoning.S016: The patient confirms she would blurt out answers before teachers even finished their sentences or called on her.
